subject: Proposal: PromptLabs / Redwood embed-sdk integration + co-marketing roadmap
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@promptlabs.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Intro + doc: co-build embed SDK shim for LangChain/LlamaIndex

Hi Soojin,

Nice to meet you over email — I’m Asha, Head of Integrations at PromptLabs. We build developer tooling for retrieval-augmented apps and customers keep asking for a first-class embedding surface that is Redwood-native (dedicated + hosted) with built-in attribution/tracing so teams can map vectors back to generation/requests.

High level ask: we'd like to propose a joint POC where PromptLabs adds a "RedwoodEmbeddingClient" shim into our LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors and also wires up call-level tracing so customers can see token-level costs and source provenance in our dashboard. In exchange PromptLabs is proposing co-marketing (blog + webinar) and early access to Redwood Dedicated for three customers.

Attached: PromptLabs-Redwood-PRD-v0.9.pdf (high-level PRD, scope, and suggested success metrics).

Can we schedule a 30-min engineer-to-engineer sync next week to validate perf/safety constraints and auth flows? Suggested technical contacts on our side: Miguel (mruiz@docforge.com) — he owns the SDK.

Thanks — Asha

--
Asha Patel
Head of Integrations, PromptLabs
asha@promptlabs.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Asha Patel <asha@promptlabs.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + doc: co-build embed SDK shim for LangChain/LlamaIndex

Hi Asha — great to meet you, and thanks for the PRD.

We’re interested. Quick notes before we sync:
- We need to confirm the auth model you expect (API key passthrough vs. short-lived tokens) — for Private customers we often require customer-controlled keys/KMS.
- Tracing request: we’ve been prototyping a trace-hook `redwood.trace.call_id` that can be emitted to observability; want to align on schema and any PII filtering.
- Performance: embedding latency targets for the connector should be < 60ms p50 for 512-d embeddings on Dedicated. If PromptLabs needs warmer caching, let’s include caching guarantees in the SOW.

I’ll loop in Rachel (product) and Jonas (runtime) to scope implementation work and propose an initial timeline. Can you do a technical call Thursday 12/3 at 10am PT? If not, toss out two other slots.

Best,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Asha Patel <asha@promptlabs.ai>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + doc: co-build embed SDK shim for LangChain/LlamaIndex — implementation sketch

Hi Asha / team — thanks for the call last week. Below is an implementation sketch and recommended milestones so we’re aligned before the SOW: 

Scope summary (what Redwood will deliver):
- redwood-embed-sdk shim (Python/TS) that implements the standard LangChain embedder interface and LlamaIndex vector store ingestion, with an option to route to Hosted vs Dedicated endpoints.
- Trace integration: a minimal HTTP header + JSON payload we can accept (call_id, request_origin, model_variant, parent_prompt_id) that will be forwarded to Redwood Console as trace events. We’ll include an opt-in PII scrub step in the shim.
- Auth modes: (A) API key passthrough for hosted customers (B) ephemeral signed tokens for Dedicated/Private. We’ll provide token issuance endpoints in the shim sample.
- Joint test harness: shared eval prompt set (10 canonical prompts) and perf bench (QPS, p50/p95 latency, mem).

Milestones & timeline (proposed):
1) 2026-12-10: SDK prototype (basic embed + auth) — dev branch
2) 2026-12-20: Trace hooks + PII scrub implemented
3) 2027-01-04: Begin 3-week joint sprint with two pilot customers (customer onboarding/kickoff)

Attachments: redwood-sdk-shim-design-20261206.md (detailed outline + API samples).

Open questions for PromptLabs:
- Will you accept our ephemeral token model for Dedicated customers, or do you need a passthrough key?
- Are there any legal/attribution requirements for vectors stored in downstream vector DBs?

We’re excited to move this forward. If the above looks good I can ask legal to craft a short SOW and shared NDA addendum for the co-marketing piece.

Thanks,
Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Product Manager, Ecosystem Integrations
redwood.com | rachel_kim@redwood.com

From: Asha Patel <asha@promptlabs.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Miguel Ruiz <mruiz@docforge.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + doc: co-build embed SDK shim for LangChain/LlamaIndex — next steps

Thanks Rachel / Soojin — this is exactly the level of detail we wanted. Miguel and I reviewed the token options and PromptLabs can support Redwood’s ephemeral token flow for Dedicated customers (preferred) and API-key passthrough for Hosted-only pilots.

We’re comfortable with the proposed milestones. Two quick asks before we sign SOW: 
1) Can Redwood include a simple demo app sample that shows end-to-end trace visualization in PromptLabs (we’ll list Redwood as the tracing source)?
2) Please include a clause in the SOW that clarifies data retention defaults for vectors (30 / 90 / custom) per customer preference — some regulated customers require configurable retention windows.

If that’s fine, we’ll route a short SOW + co-marketing addendum via DocuSign this week: https://www.docusign.com/some-doc-id/PL-ENG-SOW

Tentative go-forward: joint 3-week sprint starting 2027-01-04, two pilot customers (one Hosted, one Dedicated). Looking forward to the co-marketing webinar in March.

Best,
Asha

--
Asha Patel
Head of Integrations, PromptLabs
asha@promptlabs.ai
Attachments: PromptLabs-Redwood-PRD-v0.9.pdf (see intro section)
